verses.1: Let the streams flow together, let the winds and birds assembled come. Strengthen this sacrifice of mine, ye singers. I offer up a duly mixt oblation.
verses.2: O Burnt Oblations, aid, and ye, Blent Offerings, this my sacrifice. Strengthen this sacrifice of mine, ye singers. I offer up a duly mixt oblation.
verses.3: Each several form, each several force I seize, and compass round this man. May the Four Quarters strengthen this my sacrifice. I offer up a duly mixt oblation.
verses.4: Blest be the Streams from hills of snow, sweet be spring Waters unto thee. Sweet be swift-running Waters, sweet to thee be Water of the Rains.
verses.5: Sweet unto thee be Waters of the waste and Waters of the pool. Sweet be the Waters dug from earth, to thee, and Waters brought in jars.
verses.6: To those who delve without a tool to dig, the wise, the deeply moved, To Waters better healers than physicians we address our prayer.
verses.7: Bathed in the Waters verily divine, in water of the streams, Bathed in the Waters verily, O Horses, be ye fleet and strong.
verses.8: Blest be the Waters unto thee, suspicious Waters, bringing. health. They cure the injured place for thee even as thy comfort craveth it.
verses.9: Whithersoe'er, from sky, earth, air's mid-regions from plants ands herbs, from tall trees, Jatavedas. Is carried here and there to divers places, even thence come thou to us with loving-kindness.
verses.10: All majesty of thine in floods, in forest, in plants, in cattle, in the depths of waters Closely uniting all thy forms, O Agni, come unto us wealth-giving, undecaying.
verses.11: Thy majesty among the Gods in Svarga, thy body which hath past into the Fathers. Thy plenty far-diffused mid human beings, even with this, O Agni, give us riches.
verses.12: To him the wise, the famous, swift to listen, with words and verses I come nigh for bounty. May we be safe from threatening danger. Soften by sacrifice thewrath of Gods, O Agni.
verses.13: The first oblation that Atharvan oared, earliest sacrifice paid by Jatavedas, Even this I, foremost, with repeated worship, now offer unto thee. May Agni carry the sacrificer's present. Hail to Agni!
verses.14: In front I set Intention, blessed Goddess. Mother of thought, may she be prompt to hear us. Mine, and mine only, be the hope I fashion! May I gain this that hath possessed my spirit.
verses.15: With Purpose, O Prajapati, with Purpose come thou near to us. Bestow on us a share of luck, and so be swift to hear our call.
verses.16: Prajapati Angirasa with favour regard this word and this my settled purpose! May he, whence Gods and Deities had being Kama attend us with his gentle guidance.
verses.17: King of the living world and men is Indra, of all in varied form that earth containeth. Thence to the worshipper he giveth riches: may he enrich even us when we have praised him.
verses.18: Purusha hath a thousand arms, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet. On every side pervading earth he fills a space ten fingers wide.
verses.19: He with three quarters rose to heaven here reappeared a fourth of him. Thence he strode forth on every side to all that eats not and that eats.
verses.20: So mighty is his grandeur, yea, greater than this is Purusha. All creatures are one-fourth of him, three-fourths what dieth not in heaven.
verses.21: Purusha is in truth this All, what hath been and what yet shall; be Lord, too, of immortality--and what hath grown with somewhat else.
verses.22: When they divided Purusha how many portions did they make? What was his mouth? what were his arms? what are the names of thighs and feet?
verses.23: The Brahman was his mouth, of both his arms was the Rajanya made. His waist became the Vaisya, from his feet the Sudra was produced.
verses.24: The Moon was gendered from his mind, and from his eye the Sun had birth. Indra and Agni from his mouth were born and Vayu from his breath.
verses.25: Forth from his navel come mid-air; the sky was fashioned from his head. Earth from his feet, and from his ear the regions. Thus they formed the worlds.
verses.26: In the beginning rose Viraj: Purusha from Viraj was born. As soon as he was born he spread westward and eastward o'er the earth.
verses.27: When Gods performed the sacrifice with Purusha as their offering. Spring was the butter, summer was the fuel, autumn was the gift.
verses.28: That sacrifice, first-born Purusha, they hallowed with the sprinkled Rains. The Deities, the Sadhyas, all the Vasus sacrificed with him.
verses.29: From it were horses born, from it all creatures with two rows of teeth. From it were generated kine, from it were goats and sheep produced.
verses.30: From that great general sacrifice Richas and Sama hymns were born; Therefrom the metres were produced: the Yajus had its birth from it.
verses.31: From that great general sacrifice the dripping fat was gathered up: It formed the creatures fleet as wind, and animals both wild and tame.
verses.32: Seven fencing-logs had he, thrice seven layers of fuel were prepared. When, offering sacrifice, the Gods bound as their victim Purusha.
verses.33: Forth from head of the high God seven-and-seventy bright beams. Sprang into being, of the King Soma produced from Purusha.
verses.34: The brilliant lights shining in heaven together, which through the world glide on with rapid motion. And Days, and Firmament with songs I worship, seeking the Twenty-eight-fold for its favour.
verses.35: Krittikas, Rohini be swift to hear me! Let Mrigasiras bless me, help me Ardra! Punarvasu and Sunrita, fair Pushya, the Sun, Asleshas, Magha lead me onward!
verses.36: My bliss be Svati and benignant Chitra, my right First Phalgunis and present Hasta. Radhas, Visakhas, gracious Anuradha, Jyeshtha and happystarred uninjured Mula.
verses.37: Food shall be earlier Ashadhas grant me; let those that follow bring me strength and vigour; With virtuous merit Abhijit endow me! Sravana and Sravishthas make me prosper.
verses.38: Satabhishak afford me ample freedom, and both the Proshthapadas guard me safely. Revati and the Asvayujas bring me luck, and the Bharanis abundant riches!
verses.39: Benign to me be all those Lunar Mansions to which the Moon as he moves on doth honour. All that are in the sky, the air, the waters, on earth, on mountains, in the heavenly regions.
verses.40: Propitious, mighty, let the eight-and-twenty together deal me out my share of profit. Profit and wealth be mine, and wealth and profit! To Day and Night be adoration rendered!
verses.41: Fair be my sunset, fair my morn and evening and day with. lucky chase and happy omens; With blessing and success, immortal Agni, go to the mortal and. return rejoicing.
verses.42: Excitement and invoking cry, ill-omened sneezing and reproof, All sounds of empty pitchers send into the distance, Savitar!
verses.43: May we escape an evil sneeze, enjoy the sneeze of happy luck, And may our nostrils smelling what is pleasant pour forth fragrant scent.
verses.44: These flames of Brahmanaspati borne to all quarters in thewind, Turn them all hither, Indra, and make them most gracious unto, me.
verses.45: Let well-being be ours; let fearlessness be ours; homage be to day-and-night.
verses.46: Gentle be heaven, gentle be earth, gentle this spacious, atmosphere. Gentle be waters as they flow, gentle to us be plants and herbs!
verses.47: Gentle be signs of coming change, and that which is and is not. done! Gentle be past and future, yea, let all be gracious unto us.
verses.48: Quickened by Prayer, this Goddess Vak who standeth in the highest place, By whom the awful spell was made, even through her to us be peace!
verses.49: Or, made more keen by Prayer, this mind that standeth in the highest place, Whereby the awful spell was made, even through this be peace to us!
verses.50: These five sense-organs with the mind as sixth, sharpened by Prayer, abiding in my heart, By which the awful spell was made, even by these be peace to us.
verses.51: Favour us Mitra, Varuna, and Vishnu, and Prajapati! Gracious* to us be Indra and Brihaspati and Aryaman.
verses.52: Favour us Mitra, Varuna, Vivasvan, and the Finisher, Portents on earth and in the air, and planets wandering in heaven!
verses.53: Gracious to us be trembling earth, gracious the flaming meteor stroke! Gracious be kine who yield red milk, gracious be earth when sinking down!
verses.54: Gracious be meteor-stricken constellation, gracious to us be magic spells and witchcraft! Gracious to us be buried charms, and gracious the meteors and the portents of the region!
verses.55: Kind be the Powers who seize the Moon, with Rahu be Adityas kind! Favour us Death and Cornet, and Rudras with penetrating. might!
verses.56: Rudras and Vasus favour us, Adityas, Agnis favour us! Favour us mighty Rishis, Gods, Goddesses, and Brihaspati!
verses.57: Brahma, Dhatar, Prajapati, Worlds, Vedas, Agnis, Rishis Seven. All these have blessed my happy way. May Indra be my guardian, may Brahma protect and shelter me.
verses.58: May all the Gods protect me, may the Gods united shield me well. May all alleviations in the world which the Seven Rishis know. Be kind and gracious unto me. Bliss and security be mine!
verses.59: Earth alleviation, air alleviation, heaven alleviation, waters alleviation, plants alleviation, trees alleviation, all Gods my alleviation, collective Gods my alleviation, alleviation by alleviations. By these alleviations, these universal alleviations, I allay all that is terrific here, all that is cruel, all that is wicked. This hath been calmed, this is now auspicious. Let all be favourable to us.
verses.60: Befriend us with their aids Indra and Agni, Indra and Varuna who receive oblations! Indra and Soma give health, wealth and comfort, Indra and Pushan be our strength in battle!
verses.61: Auspicious friends to us be Bhaga. Sansa, auspicious be Purandhi and all Riches, The blessing of the true and well-conducted and Aryaman in many forms apparent.
verses.62: Kind unto us be Maker and Sustainer and the far-reaching One with godlike nature. Auspicious unto us be Earth and Heaven, the Mountain and the Gods' fair invocations.
verses.63: Favour us Agni with his face of splendour, and Varuna and' Mitra and the Asvins. Favour us noble actions of the pious; impetuous Vata blow on, us with favour!
verses.64: Early invoked may Heaven and Earth be friendly, and Air's mid-region good for us to look on. To us may herbs and forest trees be gracious, gracious the Lord victorious of the region.
verses.65: Be the God Indra with the Vasus friendly, and with Adityas Varuna who blesseth. Kind with the Rudras be the healer Rudra, and with the Dames here Tvashtar kindly hear us.
verses.66: Kind unto us be Soma and Devotions, kind be the sacrifice and Stones for pressing. Kind be the fixing of the Sacred Pillars, kind be the tender Grass, and kind the Altar.
verses.67: May the far-seeing Sun rise up to bless us: be the four quartersof the heaven auspicious. Auspicious be the firmly-seated Mountains, auspicious be the Rivers and the Waters.
verses.68: May Aditi through holy works be gracious, and may the Maruts,_ loud in song, be friendly. May Vishnu give felicity, and, Pushan, and Air that cherisheth. our lives, and Vayu.
verses.69: Prosper us Savitar, the God who rescues, and let the radiant. Mornings be propitious. Propitious to our children be Parjanya, kind to us be the field's benign Protector!
verses.70: May the great Lords of Truth protect and aid us: blest to us be our horses and our cattle. Kind be the pious, skilful-handed Ribhus, kind be the Fathers at our invocations
verses.71: Kind to us be the Gods and Visve Devas, Sarasvati with Holy Thoughts be gracious. Friendly be they, the Liberal Ones, who seek us, yea, those who dwell in-heaven, on earth, in waters.
verses.72: May Aja-Ekapad the God be gracious, gracious the Dragon of the Deep, and Ocean. Gracious be he, the swelling Child of Waters, gracious be Prisni who hath Gods to guard her.
verses.73: So may the Rudras, Vasus, and Adityas accept the new hymn we now are making. May all the Holy Ones of earth and heaven, and the Cow's offspring hear our invocation.
verses.74: Priests of the Gods, worthy of sacrifices, immortal, knowing Law, whom man must worship. May these to-day give us broad paths to travel. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
verses.75: Be it so, O Mitra-and-Varuṇa, so, O Agni: weal [and] profit for us be this praise (śastá); may we reach sounding (gādhá) and firm standing; homage to the great sky, [our] seat.
verses.76: Dawn drives away her sister's gloom, and through her excellence makes her retrace her path. Through her may we gain God-appointed treasure, and with brave sons be glad through hundred winters.
verses.77: These the two sturdy, manly arms of Indra, these that are wondrous, mighty, and successful First, when the need hath come will I employ them by which the heaven of Asuras was conquered.
verses.78: Swift, like a dread bull sharpening his weapons, rapidly striking, stirring up the people, Loud shouting, vigilant, the one sole Hero, Indra subdued a hundred hosts together.
verses.79: With him loud-roaring, ever watchful, victor bold, hard to overthrow, whom none may vanquish, Indra the strong whose hand bears arrows, conquer, ye heroes now, now vanquish in the combat.
verses.80: He rules with those who carry shafts and quivers, Indra who with his hand brings hosts together, Foe-conquering, strong of arm, the Soma-drinker, with mighty bow, shooting with well-laid arrows.
verses.81: Conspicuous by thy strength, firm, foremost fighter, mighty and fierce, victorious, all-subduing, O'ercoming might, excelling men and heroes, mount the kinewinning conquering car, O Indra.
verses.82: Troop-vanquisher, kine-winner, armed with thunder, who quells an army and with might destroys it, Follow him, comrades! quit yourselves like heroes, and like this Indra show your zeal and courage.
verses.83: Piercing the cow-stalls with surpassing vigour, Indra the pitiless hero, wild with anger, Victor in fight, unshaken and resistless,--may he protect our armies in our battles.
verses.84: Brihaspati, fly with thy chariot hither, slayer of demons, driving. off our foemen. Be thou protector of our bodies, crushing our enemies, destroying those who hate us.
verses.85: Indra guide these! Brihaspati, the Guerdon, and Soma, and the Sacrifice precede them! And let the banded Maruts march in forefront of heavenly hosts that conquer and demolish.
verses.86: Ours be the potent host of mighty Indra, King Varuna, and Maruts and Adityas. Uplifted is the shout of Gods who conquer, high-minded God who cause the world to tremble.
verses.87: May Indra aid us when our flags are gathered: victorious be th arrows of our army. May our brave men of war prevail in battle. Ye Gods, protect u in the shouts of onset.
verses.88: I have attained this goodliest place to rest in. Both Heaven and, Earth have shown me grace and favour. Without a foe for me be all the regions! We hate thee not. May we have peace and safety.
verses.89: Indra, give us security from that whereof we are afraid. Help us, O Maghavan, let thy succour grant us this: drive foes and enemies afar.
verses.90: We call on Indra, on the liberal giver: we will be prosperous in men and cattle. Let not the hosts of cruel fiends approach us. Drive of the Druhs to every side, O Indra.
verses.91: Best, making household wealth increase. Indra our saviour, kills the foe. May he from outmost point be our potector, and from the centre and from west and eastward.
verses.92: Lead us to ample room. O thou who knowest, to happiness security, and sunlight. Strong, Indra, are the arms of thee the mighty: may we betake us to their lofty shelter.
verses.93: May air's mid-region give us peace and safety, safety may both these, Heaven and Earth, afford us. Security be ours from west, from eastward, from north and south may we be free from danger.
verses.94: Safety be ours from friend and from the unfriendly, safety from what we know and what we know not. Safety be ours by night and in the day-time! friendly to me be all my hopes and wishes!
verses.95: Peace hath been given us from the east, and from the west security. Savitar guard me from the south, and from the north the Lord of Might.
verses.96: May the Adityas from the sky protect me, Agni from the earth. May Indra-Agni guard me from the eastward, on all sides may the Asvins give me shelter. May Jatavedas guard, sidelong, our cattle. Our shield on all sides be the World-Creators!
verses.97: Agni from eastward guard me with the Vasus! To him I go, in him I rest: this fort I seek for refuge. May he protect me, may he be my guardian. I give my soul--All hail! into his keeping.
verses.98: Vayu with Air protect me from this region. To him I go, etc.
verses.99: May Soma from the south, with Rudras, guard me. To him, etc.
verses.100: Varuna with Adityas guard me from this region! To him etc.
verses.101: Surya with Earth and Heaven from the western region guard me well. To him, etc.
verses.102: May Waters joined with Plants protect me from this region. To them I go, in them I rest: this fort I seek for refuge. May they protect me, may they be my guardians. I give my soul--All hail! --into their keeping.
verses.103: May Visvakarman with the Seven Rishis be my protector from the northern region. To him, etc.
verses.104: May Indra, Marut-girt, protect me from this region. To him, etc.
verses.105: Prajapati, of generative power, with the Pratishlha save me from the nadir! To him, etc.
verses.106: Brihaspati, joined by the Visvedevas, protect me from the region of the zenith! To him, I go, in him I rest; this fort I seek for refuge. May he protect me, may he be my guardian. I give my soul-- All hail!--into his keeping.
verses.107: Let those who vex me from the eastern region, sinners, praise Agni followed by the Vasus.
verses.108: Let those who vex me from this quarter, sinners, praise Vayu compassed by the Air's mid region.
verses.109: Let those who vex me from the southern quarter, sinners, sing praise to Soma with the Rudras.
verses.110: Let those who vex me from this quarter, sinners, praise Varuna connected with Adityas.
verses.111: Let those who vex me from the western quarter, sinners, praise Surya linked with Earth and Heaven.
verses.112: Let those who vex me from this quarter, sinners give praise to plants' associates the Waters.
verses.113: Let those who from the north side vex me, sinners, praise Visvakarman with the Seven Rishis.
verses.114: Let those who vex me from this quarter, sinners, praise Indra with the Marut host about him.
verses.115: Let those who vex me from the nadir, sinners, extol Prajapati of genial power.
verses.116: Let those who vex me from the zenith, sinners, extol Brihaspati with the Visve Devas.
verses.117: Mitra arose with Earth. To that fort I lead you: enter it, occupy it. Let it give you protection and defence.
verses.118: Vayu arose with Air. To that fort, etc.
verses.119: Surya arose with Heaven. To that fort, etc.
verses.120: Chandramas arose with the Constellation. To that fort, etc.
verses.121: Sacrifice arose with Priestly Fees. To that fort, etc.
verses.122: Ocean arose with the Rivers. To that fort, etc.
verses.123: Brahma arose with the Brahmacharis. To that fort, etc.
verses.124: Indra arose with Might. To that fort, etc.
verses.125: The Gods arose with Immortality. To that fort, etc.
verses.126: Prajapati arose with Creatures. To that fort I lead you: enter it, occupy it give you protection and defence.
verses.127: Prajāpati ascended with progeny: to that stronghold etc. etc.
verses.128: May Soma, Varuna the King, both Asvins, Yama and Pushan guard us well from Mrityu-- Death caused by men, which Indra-Agni, Dhatar, Brihaspati and Savitar appointed.
verses.129: All that the World's Lord made, all that for creatures Prajapati and Matarisvan fashioned, All things within the quarters and their spaces, let all these be my manifold defences.
verses.130: That which the Gods bound on them when they battled for their royal sway. What Indra made his shield, may that protect us well on every side,
verses.131: My shield is Heaven and Earth, my shield is the bright Day, my shield the Sun. The Visva Devas made my shield. Let not misfortune fall on me.
verses.132: Gayatri, Ushnih, Anushtup, Brihati, Trishtup, Jagati.
verses.133: With the first five chapters of the Angirases, Hail!
verses.135: To the seventh and eight, Hail!
verses.139: To those composed in strophes, Hail!
verses.147: To those with hair in tufts, Hail!
verses.150: To all the Vidagana Angirases, Hail!
verses.151: To those two with separate thousands, Hail!
verses.153: Collected manly powers are topped by Brahma. Brahma at first spread out the loftiest heaven. Brahma was born first of all things existing. Who then is meet to be that Brahma's rival?
verses.154: Hail to the four-verse strophes of the Atharvanas!
verses.175: Hail to the single non-Rich-versed ones!
verses.177: Hail to the two Surya hymns!
verses.178: Hail to the two Vratya hymns!
verses.179: Hail to the two Prajapati hymns!
verses.180: Hail to the hymn of victory!
verses.181: Hail to the hymns for happiness!
verses.183: Collected manly powers are topped by Brahma. Brahma at first spread out the loftiest heaven. Brahma was born first of all things existing. Who then is fit to be this Brahma's rival?
verses.184: Do ye, O Brahmanaspati, invest for the royal sway this man. With that wherewith the Deities invested Savitar the God.
verses.185: Invest this Indra for long life, invest him for great princely power, That I may lead him on to eld, that the man watch his princedom long.
verses.186: Invest this Soma for long life, invest him for great hearing power. That I may lead him on to eld, that he may watch o'er hearing long.
verses.187: For us, surround him, cover him with splendour, give him long life, and death when age removes him. This garment hath Brihaspati presented to Soma, to the King, to wrap about him.
verses.188: Advance to good old age: endue the mantle. Be thou our heifers' guard from imprecation. Live thou a hundred full and plenteous autumns, and wrap thee in prosperity of riches.
verses.189: Thou for weal hast clothed thee in this garment: thou hast become our cows' sure guard from curses. Live thou a hundred full and plenteous autumns: then living, fair thyself, shalt deal forth treasures.
verses.190: In every need, in every fray we call, as friends, to succour us, Indra the mightiest of all.
verses.191: Gold-coloured, undecaying, blest with heroes, dwell, dying in old age, with children round thee. This is the spoken word of Agni, Soma, Brihaspati and Savitar, and Indra.
verses.192: I yoke thee with the mind of one unwearied still and first of all. Be thou a bearer up the hill: run hither bearing up thy load.
verses.193: Gold that was born from Fire is immortal hath been deposited with mortal creatures. He who knows this deserves to own this jewel, and in extreme old age dies he who wears it.
verses.194: The men of ancient time with children round them longed for this Gold, bright with the Sun's own colour, This shall endow thee, as it shines, with splendour, and long shall be the life of him who wears it.
verses.195: Long life and splendour let it bring energy and strength to thee. That thou mayst shine among the folk with all the brightness of the Gold.
verses.196: What Varuna the King knows well, and what the God Brihaspati, And Indra, Slayer of the Foe, may that bestow long life on thee, may that increase thy splendid strength.
verses.197: Let the Bull guard thee with the kine, the Stallien with the fleetfoot steeds. Let Vayu keep thee safe with prayer, and Indra with his mighty power.
verses.198: Let Soma guard thee with the plants, Surya protect thee with the stars; With breath let Wind protect thee, and the Moon, foe-slayer, with the months.
verses.199: Three are the earths, they say, and three the heavens, three are the atmospheres, and four the oceans. Threefold the hymn of praise, threefold the Waters. Let these with triple song and triplets guard thee.
verses.200: Three vaults of heaven, and three seas, three bright, three stationary ones, Three Matarisvans, and three suns, protectors, I arrange for thee.
verses.201: Increasing thee with butter I, Agni! with fatness sprinkle thee. Let not magicians harm the life of Agni or of Moon or Sun.
verses.202: Let not magicians mar your heat, your vital or diffusive breath. Brilliant and all-possessing Gods, run ye your course with Godlike power.
verses.203: Fire they endow with vital breath, Wind is compact, with vital breath: With vital breath the Gods produced the Sun whose face turn every way.
verses.204: Live with the Life-Creators' life. Die not, live on to lengthened age. Live with the breath of men with souls. Submit not to the power of Death.
verses.205: The secret treasure of the Gods which Indra, by pathways travelled by the Gods, discovered, That gold the Waters with the triplets guarded. May they keep thee with threebold hymn and triplets.
verses.206: With friendly thoughts the Deities, three-and thirty, and three great Powers preserved it in the Waters. He made heroic powers with the gold that lies upon this Moon.
verses.207: O ye eleven Gods who are in heaven, accept this sacrifice.
verses.208: O ye eleven Gods who are in air, accept this sacrifice.
verses.209: O ye eleven Gods who are on earth, accept this sacrifice.
verses.210: Peace hath been given us from the east, and from the west security. Savitar guard me from the south, and from the north the Lord of Might.
verses.211: May the Adityas from the sky protect me, Agni from the earth. May Indra-Agni guard me from the eastward, on all sides may the Asvins give me shelter. May Jatavedas guard, sidelong, our cattle. Our shield on all sides be the World-Creators!
verses.212: On thee I bind this Amulet for lengthened life and brilliancy. The rival-quelling Darbha grass that burns the spirit of a foe.
verses.213: Burning the spirit of the foe, vexing the heart of enemies. Darbha, on every side, like heat, inflame all evil-hearted men.
verses.214: O Darbha, burning round like heat, consuming foes, O Amulet,. Like Indra rending Vala cleave mine adversaries' hearts in twain.
verses.215: Cleave through. O Darbha, Amulet, my foes', mine adversaries'. heart. Rise thou and batter down their heads like growth that coverethl the earth.
verses.216: Cleave thou my rivals, Darbha, cleave the men who fain would, fight with me. Cleave all who wish me evil, cleave the men who hate me,. Amulet!
verses.217: Wound thou, my rivals, Darbha, etc. (as in 5, substituting. 'wound' for cleave.)
verses.218: Tear thou my rivals, Darbha, etc.
verses.219: How thou my rivals, Darbha, etc.
verses.220: Carve thou my rivals, Darbha, etc.
verses.221: Pierce thou my rivals, Darbha, pierce the men who fain would fight with me. Pierce those who wish me evil, pierce the men who hate me, Amulet!
verses.222: Pierce thou my rivals, Darbha, pierce the men who fain would fight with me. Pierce all who wish me evil, pierce the men who hate me,. Amulet!
verses.223: Split thou my rivals, Darbha, etc. (as in 1, with 'split' for 'pierce' throughout).
verses.230: Slay thou my rivals. Darbha, slay the men who fain would fight with me. Slay all who wish me evil, slay the men who hate me, Amulet.
verses.231: Darbha, with that good shield of thine, of hundred guards tilt death in eld, Arm thou this man, and with thy might strike thou his adversaries down.
verses.232: Darbha, thou hast a hundred shields, thou hast a thousand. manly powers. All Gods have given thee to him to bear thee till extreme old age.
verses.233: They call thee, 'Darbha, shield of Gods, they call the Brahmanaspati. They call thee shield of Indra: thou protectest kingdoms from attack.
verses.234: Darbha, destroyer of the foe, vexing the hearts of enemies, An Amulet that strengthens rule I make thee, and the body's. guard.
verses.235: What time Parjanya roared to it with lightning flashes in the sea, Thence came the drop, the golden drop, thence Darbha into being sprang.
verses.236: Savitar make all cattle grow and prosper in my stable with. Amulet of Udumbara, helper of him who longs for wealth!
verses.237: May he who was our Household Fire, the ruler of our cattle, strong. Amulet of Udumbara endow us with prosperity.
verses.238: By power of the Udumbara Charm may Dhatar give me plenty, rich. In the kine's droppings and in fruit, and, in our dwelling, food, and drink.
verses.239: I win great plenty, while I wear the Amulet of Udumbara. Of quadrupeds and bipeds, of juices and food of every sort.
verses.240: I have obtained abundant wealth of cattle, bipeds and quadrupeds, and corn in plenty. Savitar and Brihaspati vouchsafe me the milk of kine and herbs' refreshing juices!
verses.241: Fain would I be the lord of herds of cattle: may he who rules o'er riches send me riches! May the Udumbara Amulet vouchsafe possessions unto me.
verses.242: To me with wealth and children come the Amulet of Udumbara. With splendour come the Amulet hastened by Indra on its way!
verses.243: Divine, foe-quelling Amulet, wealth-winner for the gain of wealth-- May it give store of beasts and food and cause our kine to multiply.
verses.244: As thou, O Forest Tree, wast born with increase when thy life began, So let Sarasvati bestow abundant growth of wealth on me.
verses.245: Sarasvati vouchsafe me wealth, household prosperity, and corn! Let Sinivali bring them, and this Amulet of Udumbara.
verses.246: The Lord of amulets art thou, most mighty: in thee wealth's ruler hath engendered riches, These gains are lodged in thee, and all great treasures. Amulet, conquer thou: far from us banish malignity and indigence, and hunger.
verses.247: Vigour art thou, in me do thou plant vigour: riches art thou, so do thou grant me riches. Plenty art thou, so prosper me with plenty: House-holder, hear" a householder's petition.
verses.248: Amulet of Udumbara, enrich us: vouchsafe us wealth with all good men about us. I bind thee on for increase of possessions.
verses.249: For hero is this hero bound, Amulet of Udumbara. So may he make our offering sweetly-savoured, and grant us wealth with all good men about us.
verses.250: For lengthened life I bind on thee the Darbha grass, the mighty plant. Excellent, hard to overthrow, with hundred stems and thousand blades.
verses.251: They cut not off his hair, they strike blow upon the breast for' him. To whom one gives protection by Darbha that hath uninjured leaves.
verses.252: O Plant, thy root is in the sky, and thou art stationed on the earth: With thee who hast a thousand stalks we strengthen all the powers of life.
verses.253: Through all three skies the plant hath pierced, and the three regions of the earth; With thee I split in twain the tongue and words of the badhearted man.
verses.254: Thou art victorious in thy might I am endowed with conquering strength: Possessed of overpowering force we two will quell our enemies.
verses.255: Subdue our foeman, overcome the men who fain would fight: with us. Conquer all evil-hearted ones: make many well-disposed to me.
verses.256: With Darbha that hath sprung from Gods, stationed in heaven, full many a time. With this have I won many men, have won and may I win them still.
verses.257: Do thou, O Darbha, make me dear to Brahman and Rajanya, dear to Sudra, and to Arya dear, Yea, dear to every man we love, to every man with eyes to see.
verses.258: He who first born fixed earth in her position, he who established heaven and air's mid-region, Whom sinner ne'er hath known as his supporter,--this Darbha be our shelter and protection!
verses.259: First of all plants it sprang into existence, victorious, hundredstemmed, the foe-subduer, So may this Darbha from all sides protect us: with this may I subdue our foes in battle.
verses.260: Hundred stemmed, succulent, and worth a thousand, the Royal Rite of plants, the Water's Agni, Let this same Darbha guard us from all quarters. This Godlike Amulet shall with life endow us.
verses.261: Drawn forth from butter, juicy, sweetly-flavoured, firm as the earth, unshaken, overthrowing. Driving off foes and casting them beneath me, mount with the strength of mighty Ones, O Darbha.
verses.262: Thou movest o'er the earth with vigour: lovely in sacrifice thou sittest on the altar. The Rishis bear thee as a purifier: cleanse thou us from all evil deeds' defilement.
verses.263: A stern and all-victorious king, foe-queller, dear to every man-- That energy of Gods and mighty power, I bind this on thee for long life and welfare.
verses.264: Achieve heroic deeds with Darbha, wearing this Darbha never let thy soul be troubled. In splendour and precedence over others illumine like the Sun the heaven's four regions.
verses.265: Jangida, thou art Angiras: thou art a guardian, Jangida. Let Jangida, keep safely all our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
verses.266: Dice-witcheries, the fifty-threes, the hundred witchcraft-practisers, All these may Jangida make weak, bereft of their effectual force.
verses.267: Baffle the loud factitious howl, make impotent the seven decays. As when an archer speeds the shaft, drive away want, O Jangida,
verses.268: This counteracts the sorceress, this banishes malignity: Then may victorious Jangida's prolong the days we have to live.
verses.269: Let Jangida's protecting might encompass us on every side. Wherewith he quells Vishkandha and Sanskandha, might by greater might.
verses.270: Three times the Gods engendered thee fixt on the surface of the earth; The Brahmans of the olden time knew that thy name was Angiras;
verses.271: The ancient plants surpass thee not, nor any herbs of recent days. A potent charm is Jangida, a most felicitous defence.
verses.272: Then when thou sprangest into life, Jangida of un-measured strength, Indra, O mighty One, bestowed great power upon thee from the first.
verses.273: To thee in truth, O Forest Tree, Indra the mighty One gave strength. Driving away all maladies, strike thou the demons down, O Plant.
verses.274: Lumbago and rheumatic pain, consumptive cough, and pleurisy, And fever which each Autumn brings, may Jangida makepowerless.
verses.275: While their lips uttered Indra's name the Rishis gave us Jangida.. Which in the earliest time Gods made a remedy, Vishkandha'scure.
verses.276: So may this Jangida guard us, even as a treasurer guards wealth,. Even this which Gods and Brahmans made a malice-quelling sure defence.
verses.277: Hard-hearted men, the cruel eye, the sinner who hath come tous, Destroy thou these with watchful care, O thou who hast a. thousand eyes. Thou, Jangida, art my defence.
verses.278: Guard me from earth and guard me from the heavens, guard me from middle air, from plants protect me. Protect me from the present and the future. From every region Jangida preserve us!
verses.279: All sorcerers made by the Gods, all that arise from mortal men,. These, one and all, let Jangida, healer of all, make impotent.
verses.280: The Hundred-haired hath banished hence fiends and Consumptions by its might. With splendour hath the charm that scares demons of ill-name mounted up.
verses.281: It drives off demons with its horns and sorceresses with its root, It stays Consumption with its waist: from this no wickedness escapes.
verses.282: Consumptions, light and serious, and those which sounds accompany, All these the Amulet, Hundred-haired, scarer of fiends, hath banished hence.
verses.283: A hundred men hath it produced, hundred Consumptions chased away, All fiends of evil-name it hath smitten, and shakes the Rakshasas.
verses.284: The Bull that weareth horns of gold, this Amulet with hundred hairs, Hath cleft the demons of ill-name and overcome the Rakshasas.
verses.285: Hundred she-fiends, a hundred of Gandharvas and Apsarasas, A hundred of dog-mated nymphs, I keep away with Hundred- Hair
verses.286: To me hath come this word given by Agni, fame, force and might, and strength, and life, and lustre. May Agni too bestow on me three-times a hundred manly powers.
verses.287: For mighty strength, for action, I receive thee, for manly power, to last a hundred autumns.
verses.288: For conquering strength and energy and vigour I fasten thee for chieftainship, for bearing royal dominion through a hundred autumns.
verses.289: With Seasons and with Season-groups, for vigour and extended life. With splendour of the perfect year we fasten thee about the neck.
verses.290: Never Consumption, never curse touches the man, Arundhati! Whom the delicious odour of the healing Bdellium penetrates
verses.291: Consumptions flee apart from it as from a wild beast fly the deer. If thou, O Bdellium, art produced from Sindhu or hast come from sea, The quality of both have I taken to keep this man unscathed.
verses.293: Let Kushtha from the Hill of Snow come, a divine deliverer. Banish thou all Consumption, drive all sorceresses far away.
verses.294: Kushtha, three several names hast thou, Naghamara, Nagharisha: let not mishap befall this man, For whom I make a charm of thee at eve, at morning, and by day.
verses.295: Jivala is thy mother's name, thy father's name is Jivala; let not mishap, etc.
verses.296: Thou art the best amid the plants, even as the ox is best of tame, the tiger of rapacious beasts: let not mishap, etc.
verses.297: Born thrice from the Adityas, thrice from Bhrigus, thrice from Angiras' sons, born from the Visve Devas thrice, Healer of every malady, that Kushtha stands by Soma's side. Banish thou all Consumption, drive all sorceresses far away.
verses.298: In the third heaven above us stands the Asvattha tree, the seat of Gods: There is embodiment of life that dies not: thence was Kushtha born.
verses.299: There moved through heaven a golden ship, a ship with cordage wrought of gold: There is embodiment of life that dies not; thence was Kushtha born.
verses.300: Where is the Sinking of the Ship, the summit of the Hill of Snow, There is embodiment of life that dies not: thence was Kustha born. Healer of every malady, that Kushtha stands by Soma's side. Banish thou all Consumption, drive all sorceresses far away.
verses.301: Thou whom Ikshvaku's ancestor, whom he who well-loved Kushtha, knew, Whom Vayasa and Matsya knew, hence healer of all ills art thou.
verses.302: O thou who hast all-reaching might drive away Fever, drive it down, racking Fever, tertian, continual, lasting for a year.
verses.303: For each defect of mine in voice and spirit I have approached One vehement and ardent. With all the Deities, fully approving, Brihaspati supply the want!
verses.304: Disturb ye not our intellect, O Waters, nor the power of prayer_ Glide on your way, strength-giving, invocated: may I be vigorous and wise.
verses.305: Mar not our consecrating rite, our intellect, or fervent zeal. Gracious to us for lengthened life, propitious let the Mothers be.
verses.306: Vouchsafe to us, ye Asvins twain, such strength as, with attendant light, May through the darkness carry us.
verses.307: Desiring bliss, at first, light-finding Rishis began religious rite and holy fervour. Thence energy was born, and might, and kingship: so to this man let gathered Gods incline them.
verses.308: Brahma is Hotar, sacrifice: with Brahma are the stakes set up. From Brahma was the Adhvaryu born, from Brahma hidden offering.
verses.309: Brahma is fatness-dropping scoops: with Brahma was the altar reared. Brahma is worship, lengthened rite, the Rishis who pay sacrifice, the victim's Immolators. Hail!
verses.310: To him who frees from woe mine hymn I offer, to the Good Guardian, as I seek his favour. Accept this offering of mine, O Indra. Fulfilled be all the sacrificer's wishes!
verses.311: With prayer I call on him who frees from trouble, Prince of Gods, Splendid, chief of sacrifices, I call the Waters' Child and both the Asvins, Vigour is mine, and strength bestowed by Indra.
verses.312: Whither men versed in Brahma go, with fervour and the cleansing rite, Thither let Agni lead me, let Agni give me intelligence, All hail to Agni!
verses.313: Whither etc. Thither let Vayu lead me, let Vayu vouchsafe me vital breath. All hail to Vayu!
verses.314: Whither, etc. Thither let Surya lead me, let Surya vouchsafe me power of sight. All hail to Surya
verses.315: Whither, etc. Thither let Chandra lead me, let Chandra vouchsafe me intellect. All hail to Chandra!
verses.316: Whither, etc. Thither let Soma lead me, let Soma vouchsafe me vital sap. All hail to Soma!
verses.317: Whither, etc. Thither let Indra lead me, let Indra bestow upon me power. All hail to Indra!
verses.318: Whither, etc. Thither, let Waters lead me, let the Waters give me deathless life. All hail to Waters!
verses.319: Whither, etc. Thither let Brahma lead me, let Brahma give Brahma unto me. All hail to Brahma!
verses.320: Thou art the lengthening of life, thy name is Universal Cure: Then, Ointment! send felicity; Waters, send happiness and peace.
verses.321: The yellow hue, the feverish heat, the shooting pain that rends II the limbs, All the consumptive malady let the Ointment drive from out thy frame.
verses.322: Let the Salve born upon the earth, benignant, giving life to man. Make the swift rider on the car sinless, exempt from sudden death.
verses.323: Preserve our breath, O Vital Breath, have mercy on our life, O Life. From snares of Nirriti do thou, O Nirriti, deliver us.
verses.324: Thou art the babe of Sindhu, thou art lightnings' flower, wind, breath, and Sun: thou art the eye and milk of heaven.
verses.325: Gods' Ointment from the Three Peaked Hill, preserve thou me on every side. No plants of earth surpass thee, none from mountain or from cultured ground.
verses.326: Now hath it gently crept within, fiend-slaying, chasing malady. And driving all diseases hence, and evil omens, banished them.
verses.327: Full many a falsehood, O thou King Varuna, man hath uttered here: Do thou who hast a thousand powers preserve us from that misery.
verses.328: If we have cried, O Waters! Cows! if we have cried, O Varuna! For this endowed with thousand powers! deliver us from misery.
verses.329: Mitra and Varuna, O Salve have closely followed after thee May they, when they have followed thee afar, restore thee for our use.
verses.330: As debt from debt repay and send sorcery to the sorcerer's house. Split, Salve! the cruel villain's ribs whose evil eye bewitches us.
verses.331: Whatever evil dream we have, what'er befall our kine or home, Be this that is salubrity, the evil-hearted's foe applied.
verses.332: Increasing from the Waters' strength and vigour, sprung into life from Agni Jatavedas, Strong as four heroes, mountain born, this Ointment make for thee quarters and mind-points auspicious!
verses.333: On thee is laid the Chaturvira Ointment: let all the regions give thee peace and safety. Secure like precious Savitar thou standest: to thee let all these regions bring their tribute.
verses.334: Make one thy salve, thine amulet another, drink one, and with another bathe thy body. So let the Chaturvira keep us guarded from the four bonds of Nirriti and Grahi.
verses.335: May Agni protect me with fire for inspiration and expiration, for strength, for energy, for vigour, for weal and prosperity. All Hail!
verses.336: May Indra protect me with his Indra-power for inspiration, etc.
verses.337: May Soma protect me with Soma-power, etc.
verses.338: May Bhaga with good fortune protect me, etc.
verses.339: May the Maruts protect me with their troops for inspiration and expiration, for strength, for energy, for vigour, for weal and prosperity. All Hail!
verses.340: For manly strength Prajapati bound thee on first, invincible. This for long life on thee I bind for splendour, strength, and energy. Invincible, let it guard thee well.
verses.341: Erect, invincible, be this man's watchful keeper: let not the Panis or the sorcerers harm thee. Shake off thy foes as Indra scattered Dasyus: quell all enemies. Invincible, let it guard thee well.
verses.342: Indra hath lent the power of sight, and vital breath and strength to this. Whom even a hundred combatants, striking, have failed to overcome. Invincible, let it guard thee well.
verses.343: Around thy limbs I place the mail of Indra who hath become the Gods' imperial Sovran. Again let all the Deities bring thee hither. Invincible let it guard thee well.
verses.344: One and a hundred manly powers, a thousand lives hath this Amulet, unconquered ever. Go forth a tiger, strike down all thy foemen: let him who would oppose fall low beneath thee. Invincible, let it guard thee well.
verses.345: Drawn forth from butter, rich in milk and sweetness, hundredlived, thousand-homed, bestowing vigour, Kindly, delightsome, full of sap, and mighty, invincible let it guard thee well.
verses.346: That thou mayst be pre-eminent, slayer of rivals, rivalless, May Savitar cause thee to be chief and controller of thy kin. Invincible, let it guard thee well.
verses.347: Night! the terrestrial realm hath been filled with the Father's power and might. Thou spreadest forth on high unto the seats of Heaven: darkness that strikes with awe comes near.
verses.348: Each moving thing finds rest in her whose yonder boundary is not seen, nor that which keeps her separate. O spacious, darksome Night, may we uninjured reach the end of thee, reach, O thou blessed One, thine end.
verses.349: Thy ninety-nine examiners, O Night, who look upon mankind, Eighty-and-eight in number, or seven-and-seventy are they.
verses.350: Sixty-and-six, O opulent, fifty-and-five, O happy One, Forty-and-four and thirty-three are they, O thou enriched with spoil.
verses.351: Twenty-and-two hast thou, O Night, eleven, yea, and fewer still. With these protectors guard us well. O Daughter of the Sky, today.
verses.352: Let not a fiends or spiteful man, let no ill-wisher master us. Let not the robber seize our cows, nor the wolf take our sheep today.
verses.353: Let not the thief, O Blessed, seize our horses, nor she-fiends our men. Let thief and robber run away on pathways most remote from us.
verses.354: Far from us let Rope with Fangs, far from us let the wicked flee. Do thou make blind and headless. Night, the serpent with his pungent breath.
verses.355: Crush the wolf's jaws in pieces, strike the robber dead against a post. In thee, O Night, do we abide: we here will sleep. Be watchful thou.
verses.356: Then all that we accumulate, all that the treasure-chest contains,. All this do we entrust to thee.
verses.357: Entrust thou us to Dawn, O Mother Night. May Dawn entrust us to the Day, and Day to thee, O splendid. One.
verses.358: Whatever flying thing be here, whatever thing that creeps and. crawls. Whatever fastens on a joint, therefrom do thou protect us, Night.
verses.359: So guard thou us from west and east, protect us from the north and south. O splendid One, preserve us: we, the singers of thy praise, are here.
verses.360: They who are followers of Night, and they who watch o'er living things. They who protect all cattle, they keep watch and ward over our lives, over our herds keep watch and ward.
verses.361: Verily, Night, I know thy name, Dropper of Fatness art thou called. Thee Bharadvaja knew as such: as such be watchful o'er our wealth.
verses.362: Friend of the home, the strong and youthful maiden, Night, dear to Savitar the God, and Bhaga, All-compassing, all-glorious, prompt to listen, hath with her greatness filled the earth and heaven.
verses.363: Over all depths hath she gone up, and mounted, most mighty One, the sky's exalted summit. Over me now the loving Night is spreading with her auspicious. Godlike ways like Mitra.
verses.364: Excellent, high-born, blissful, meet for worship, Night, thou hast come: stay here with friendly spirit. Guard us, the food for men that we have gotten, and all prosperity that comes of cattle.
verses.365: With eager haste hath Night assumed the vigour of leopard,. tiger, or of tawny lion, The horse's neighing and the wild-man's bellow, Thou takest many a form when thou appearest.
verses.366: Kind through the Night be absence of the sunshine: Mother of Frost, may she be swift to hear us. Take notice of the hymn, thou highly favoured, wherewith I worship thee in all the regions.
verses.367: Even as a King, O splendid Night, thou takest pleasure in our hymn. May we through Mornings as they flush have all our good men, round us, and become possessors of all wealth.
verses.368: Yes, Ramya is the name thou hast assumed. The men who fain. would spoil. My wealth do thou annoy, O Night, that not one robber may appear, none may a second time appear.
verses.369: Thou like a well-wrought cup, O Night, art lovely: thou, a. young maid, art formed in perfect beauty. Thou lovingly, for me with eyes to se: them, hast bound on thee heaven's stars as thine adornment.
verses.370: Whatever robber comes to-day, mischievous mortal enemy. Let Night go forth, encounter him, and smite away his neck and head;
verses.371: His feet that he may walk no more, his hands that he may do no harm. The robber who comes hitherward goes crushed and mutilated hence, Goes hence, goes far away from us, goes hence and bears no spoil away.
verses.372: Blind him and make him headless, Night! the serpent with the pungent breath. Strike from his head the wolf's two eyes, and dash the thief against a post.
verses.373: Those oxen that are thine, O Night, with sharpened horns and rapid pace, With those transport us safe to-day o'er difficulties everywhere.
verses.374: Uninjured in our bodies may we pass through each succeeding night, And let malignities fail to pass, as men without a boat the depth.
verses.375: As millet hurried through the air before us is beheld no more. So cause the man to vanish, Night, who plans to do us injury.
verses.376: The thief hast thou kept far away, the robber driver of our kine. Even him who having covered up the horse's head would lead him off.
verses.377: If dealing treasure thou hast come to-day, O highly favoured Night. Cause thou us to enjoy it all so that this may not pass away.
verses.378: Do thou entrust us to the Dawn, all of us free from sin, O Night. May Dawn deliver us to Day, and Day to thee, O glorious One.
verses.379: Undisturbed am I, undisturbed is my soul, undisturbed mine eye, undisturbed mine ear, undisturbed is mine in-breathing, undisturbed mine out-breathing, undisturbed my diffusivebreath, undisturbed the whole of me.
verses.380: Under the impulse of the God Savitar, sent forth from the armsof the Asvins and both hands of Pushan I have taken thee.
verses.381: Thereafter rose Desire in the beginning, Desire the primal seed and germ of Spirit. O Kama dwelling with the lofty Kama, give growth of riches to the sacrificer.
verses.382: Thou, Kama, art victorious, famous, potent, splendid, a friend. to him who seeks thy friendship. Mighty and overpowering in battle, give strength and vigour to the sacrificer.
verses.383: They heard his prayers, and they begot, by Kama, heavenlylight for him. Who from a distance longed for it, a dealer ready to exchange.
verses.384: O Kama, with whatever wish we make this offering to thee, May it be all fulfilled to us. Then taste this sacrifice, All hail!
verses.385: Desiring what, O desire, we make to thee this oblation, let that all succeed with us; then eat (vī) thou of this oblation: hail!
verses.386: Prolific, thousand-eyed, and undecaying, a horse with seven reins Time bears us onward. Sages inspired with holy knowledge mount him: his chariot wheels are all the worlds of creatures.
verses.387: This Time hath seven rolling wheels and seven naves immorality is the chariot's axle. This Time brings hitherward all worlds about us: as primal Deity is he entreated.
verses.388: On Time is laid an overflowing beaker: this we behold in many a place appearing. He carries from us all these worlds of creatures. They call him Kala in the loftiest heaven.
verses.389: He only made the worlds of life, he only gathered the worlds of living things together. Their son did he become who was their Father: no other higher power than he existeth.
verses.390: Kala created yonder heaven, and Kala made these realms of earth. By Kala, stirred to motion, both what is and what shall be expand.
verses.391: Kala created land; the Sun in Kala hath his light and heat. In Kala rest all things that be: in Kala doth the eye discern.
verses.392: In Kala mind, in Kala breath, in Kala name are fixt and joined. These living creatures, one and all, rejoice when Kala hath approached.
verses.393: Kala embraces Holy Fire, the Highest, Brahma in himself. Yea, Kala, who was father of Prajapati, is Lord of All.
verses.394: He made, he stirred this universe to motion, and on him it rests. He, Kala, having now become Brahma, holds Parameshthin up.
verses.395: Kāla created living things and, first of all, Prajāpati. From Kāla self-made Kasyapa, from Kāla Holy Fire was born.
verses.396: From Kala sprang the Waters, sprang the regions, Brahma, Holy Fire. The Sun ascends by Kala, and in Kala sinks again to rest.
verses.397: By Kala freshly blows the wind, mighty through Kala is the Earth: on Kala rests the mighty Sky.
verses.398: In Kala erst the text produced what is and what is yet to be. From Kala sprang the Richas, and from Kala was the Yajus born.
verses.399: They formed in Kala sacrifice, eternal portion for the Gods. In Kala the Gandharvas and Apsarasas and worlds abide.
verses.400: Atharvan and this Angiras in Kala are supreme o'er heaven. Both this world and the world that is most lofty, the pure worlds and pure intermediate spaces,--
verses.401: Bringing, as 'twere, with care unceasing fodder night after night to feed this stabled Courser, Joying in food and in the growth of riches, may we thy neighbours, Agni, ne'er be injured.
verses.402: Here is thine own desire for wealth: through this be gracious unto us. Joying in food and in the growth of riches, may we thy neighbours, Agni, ne'er be injured.
verses.403: Each eve that comes our household's Lord is Agni, showing his. loving-kindness every morning. Bestow upon us treasure after treasure: enkindling thee may we increase thy body.
verses.404: Each morn that comes our household's Lord is Agni, showing. his loving-kindness every evening. Vouchsafe us treasure after treasure: kindling thee may we prosper through a hundred winters.
verses.405: Never may I come short of food to feed me. Glory to Agni, Rudra, the consumer and the Lord of food!
verses.406: Protect my company, protect its courteous members, courteous. God! Only through thee, O much-invoked, may I be ever rich in kine.
verses.407: Thou art come hither from the world of Yama: thou, resolute, affectest men with rapture. Thou, Sleep, created in the Asura's dwelling, goest, well-knowing, with the solitary.
verses.408: At first the all-containing, depth beheld thee, ere Night was born, when only Day existed. Thence hast thou come, thence, Sleep, hast thou come hither, concealing, deep within, all form and figure.
verses.409: Come from the Asuras in lofty, glory, he hath approached the Gods in search of greatness. Winners of heavenly light, the Three-and-Thirty endowed this Sleep with his supreme dominion.
verses.410: Of him nor Fathers nor the Gods have knowledge, the Gods whose gentle talk is still about him. Urged by command of Varuna the Adityas, Heroes, transported Sleep to Trita Aptya.
verses.411: Thou whose severity hath reached ill-doers, and whose reward the good have gained in slumber, Delightest heaven with thy most lofty kinship, born from his spirit who was worn and weary.
verses.412: Of old we know all places whence thou comest. O Sleep, we know him who is here thy ruler. Protect us here illustrious with glory. Go, from afar, with poisons, into distance.
verses.413: As men discharge the utmost debt, collect the eighth and sixteenth part, So to the foeman we transfer together all the evil dream.
verses.414: Princes came together, debts came together, Kushthas came together, Sixteenths came together. The whole evil dream that hath visited us we send away as a bad dream to the man who hates us.
verses.415: Child of Gods' Consorts, minister of Yama is the good Dream: that which is my trouble we drive away to the enemy.
verses.416: Thou whose name is Rough art the mouth of the Black Bird. As such we know thee, Dream, as such we know thee well. Like a horse art thou, O Dream. As they bind girth and surcingle on a horse, so bind the alien mischief-maker, the scorner of the Gods.
verses.417: The evil dream that threatens us, threatens our cattle or our home. That let the scorner of the Gods, the alien mischief-maker bind as a gold jewel round his neck.
verses.418: Still equal be the flow of butter ever causing the Year to prosper with oblation. Still be our hearing, sight, and breath uninjured: let us lose nothing of our life and vigour.
verses.419: Let lively breath invite us: we call vital breath to visit us. Earth and air's middle realm have gathered, Soma, Brihaspati and Dhartar gathered vigour.
verses.420: The earth and heaven have come to be two gatherers up of vigorous might. So let us gather vigour up and closely follow after Earth. With glory come the cows and stand beside the master of the herd. Let us when we have gathered fame and glory closely follow Earth.
verses.421: Prepare the cow-stall, for there drink your heroes: stitch ye the coats of armour wide and many. Make iron forts defying all assailants: let not your pitcher leak; stay it securely.
verses.422: The eye of sacrifice, source and beginning with voice, car, spirit unto him I offer. To this our sacrifice, wrought by Visvakarman, may the Gods come gracious and kindly-hearted.
verses.423: Let the Gods' Priests and those who merit worship, to whom oblation as their share is offered, Come to this holy service with their Consorts, and all Gods revel in the food we bring them.
verses.424: God among mortals, Agni, thou art guard of holy Law, thou art To be adored in sacred rites.
verses.425: When, ignorant, we violate the statutes of you, O Deities, with whom is knowledge, Wise Agni shall correct our faults and failings, and Soma who hath entered into Brahmans.
verses.426: To the Gods' pathway have we come desiring to execute what work we may accomplish. Let Agni--for he knows--complete the worship. He is the Priest: let him fix rites and seasons.
verses.427: May I have voice in my mouth, breath in my nostrils, sight in mine eyes, hearing in mine ears, hair that hath not turned gray, teeth free from yellowness, and much strength in mine arms.
verses.428: May I have power in my thighs, swiftness in my legs, stedfastness in my feet. May all my members be uninjured and my soul unimpaired.
verses.429: May my self remain in my body: may I enjoy the full time of life, Rest thee pleasantly: pour forth abundance, purifying thyself in Svarga.
verses.430: Make me beloved among the Gods, beloved among the Princes, make Me dear to everyone who sees, to Sudra and to Aryan man.
verses.431: Rise up, O Brahmanaspati; awake the Gods with sacrifice. Strengthen the Sacrificer: aid life, breath, and off-spring, cattle, fame.
verses.432: For lofty Jatavedas I have brought the fuel hither first. May he who knoweth all bestow faith and intelligence on me.
verses.433: With fuel and with flaming wood we, Jatavedas, strengthen thee; So do thou strengthen us in turn with children and with store of wealth.
verses.434: Whatever even be the logs which, Agni, we lay down for thee, propitious be it all to me: accept it, O most youthful God.
verses.435: Agni, these logs are thine: with these be, fain to burn! a flaming brand. Vouchsafe us length of life and give us hope of immortality.
verses.436: A Golden Eagle thou hast soared with light to heaven. Those who would harm thee as thou fliest skyward. Beat down, O Jatavedas, with thy fury. The strong hath feared: to heaven mount up with light, O Surya.
verses.437: The Asuras with iron nets, magicians, who roam about with hooks and bonds of iron, With wrath I make thy thralls, O Jatavedas. Come as a bolt foequelling, thousand pointed.
verses.438: A hundred autumns may we see.
verses.439: A hundred autumns may we live.
verses.440: A hundred autumns may we know.
verses.441: A hundred autumns may we grow.
verses.442: A hundred autumns may we thrive.
verses.443: A hundred autumns may we be.
verses.444: A hundred autumns may we bide.
verses.445: A hundred, yea, and even more.
verses.446: Both of broad and narrow I with magic power unclose the mouth. With these when we have raised the bunch of grass we pay the holy rites.
verses.447: Ye are alive. I fain would live. I fain would live my complete term of life.
verses.448: Ye live dependent. I fain would live dependent. I fain would live my complete term of life.
verses.449: Ye remain alive. I fain would remain alive. I fain would live my complete term of life.
verses.450: Ye are life-givers. I fain would live. I fain would live my complete term of life.
verses.451: Live, Indra. Live Surya. Live, ye Gods. I fain would live. Fain would I live my complete term of life.
verses.452: Let my libations, giving boons, adoring, further the Twice-born's song that honours Soma. Go ye to Brahma's world having enriched me with life and breath, with children and with cattle, with fame and wealth, and with a Brahman's lustre.
verses.453: Within the chest whence we before extracted the bunch of grass, this do we now deposit. Wrought is the sacrifice by power of Brahma. Through this assist me here, ye God, with Fervour.
